subject: Estimated means are in the opposite direction in simulation

messages.author: 6fb6fd6543d77a99
messages.subject: Estimated means are in the opposite direction in simulation
parts:
Dear all,

I ran a simulation involving a 2 manifest-variable model varying skewness, kurtosis and n at each iteration. The estimated means from the output were all negative despite the population parameters being positive. I am not sure what is happening and hope that someone can enlighten me. By the way, i can't seem to attach the codes and output. Is there a way for me to do that?

Cheers,
Yonghao

messages.author: af82fa98896529e2
messages.subject: Re: Estimated means are in the opposite direction in simulation
parts:
Hi Yonghao,

It might be a problem of factor indeterminacy. Imagine that you have one solution with factor loadings of 0.7, 0.6, and 0.5. The similar solution could be one with factor loadings of -0.7, -0.6, and -0.5 (with exactly the same fit). Since the factor means are implied from those factor loadings, the directions between two means could be reversed. What you could do is to set a constraint on factor loadings

script <- "f1 =~ load1*x1 + load2*x2 + load3*x3
load1 > 0"

or to use marker-variable method to make sure that loadings are positive.

Sunthud

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Estimated means are in the opposite direction in simulation
parts: I found the same thing, even without skew or kurtosis.  Likewise, when you make the intercepts negative, they come out positive:

pop.model <- '
x1 ~~ 0.4*x2
x1 ~~ 1*x1
x2 ~~ 1*x2

x1 ~ -0.5*1
x2 ~ -0.5*1
'
anal.model <- 'x1 ~~ x2'
dat <- simulateData(pop.model, meanstructure = TRUE, sample.nobs = 1000,
                    skewness = 0, kurtosis = 0)
fitted(sem(pop.model))
cor(dat)
colMeans(dat)
fit <- sem(anal.model, dat, meanstructure = TRUE)
summary(fit)

I don't think this is related to factor indeterminacy, but I don't have any better ideas.

Terry

messages.author: 6fb6fd6543d77a99
messages.subject: Re: Estimated means are in the opposite direction in simulation
parts:
Hi Terry,

Thank you for validating what i am observing. It seems like the problem comes from data generation (using simulateData) rather than model fitting as the data generated are already in opposite direction. Is this a bug?

I tried it with a simple one-factor CFA model and the means turn up okie.

pop.model <- '
f =~ 0.8*x1 + 0.8*x2 + 0.8*x3
f ~~ 1*f
f ~ 0.5*1
x1 ~~ 0.36*x1
x2 ~~ 0.36*x2
x3 ~~ 0.36*x3
'

my.df <- simulateData(pop.model, sample.nobs=1000)

fitted(sem(pop.model))
cor(my.df)
colMeans(my.df)

model <- '
f =~ x1 + x2 + x3'

fit <- sem(model, data=my.df, meanstructure=TRUE)
summary(fit)

Cheers,
Yonghao

messages.author: af82fa98896529e2
messages.subject: Re: Estimated means are in the opposite direction in simulation
parts: I agree that it is a bug. When the data are generated manually by the mvrnorm function, the direction is negative as expected:

pop.model <- '
x1 ~~ 0.4*x2
x1 ~~ 1*x1
x2 ~~ 1*x2
x1 ~ -0.5*1
x2 ~ -0.5*1
'
anal.model <- 'x1 ~~ x2'
dat <- simulateData(pop.model, meanstructure = TRUE, sample.nobs = 1000,
                    skewness = 0, kurtosis = 0)

library(MASS)                   
dat2 <- data.frame(mvrnorm(1000, c(-0.5, -0.5), matrix(c(1, 0.4, 0.4, 1), 2, 2)))
colnames(dat2) <- c("x1", "x2")

fitted(sem(pop.model))
cor(dat)
colMeans(dat)
fit <- sem(anal.model, data=dat, meanstructure = TRUE)
summary(fit)
cor(dat2)
colMeans(dat2)
fit2 <- sem(anal.model, data=dat2, meanstructure = TRUE)
summary(fit2)

Sunthud

messages.subject: Re: Estimated means are in the opposite direction in simulation
parts:
Yonghao,

Interesting that it wasn't a problem when specifying a CFA.

FYI, you may be interested in another R package called simsem that utilizes lavaan for analysis, but automates the process for SEM simulations. For the version on CRAN, you must specify LISREL matrices for the data generation and analysis models, but Sunthud recently added capability to use lavaan syntax instead.  These new features are still in beta testing, so he doesn't want to advertise it on this message board yet, but if you send me an email, I can send you a short example script that can get you started with installation and use.

Terry (tdj "at" ku "dot" edu)
